questions.q: Diethyl malonate reacts with acrolein (CH₂=CHCHO) in the presence of sodium ethoxide. The Michael adduct is:
questions.explain: The malonate carbanion adds to the β-carbon (the CH₂= end), and the enolate formed tautomerises back to the aldehyde. The C=O is kept and the C=C becomes single; the allylic alcohol would be the 1,2-adduct.

questions.q: Which nucleophile usually adds 1,2 (to the C=O carbon) rather than 1,4 to methyl vinyl ketone?
questions.explain: Strongly basic, hard nucleophiles such as Grignard reagents usually attack the C=O directly. Stabilised (soft) carbanions from malonates, β-keto esters and nitroalkanes are classic Michael donors.

questions.q: Ethyl acetoacetate adds to methyl vinyl ketone with NaOEt. The product, CH₃COCH(COOEt)CH₂CH₂COCH₃, has which relationship between its two ketone carbonyls?
questions.explain: The donor's α-carbon bonds to the acceptor's β-carbon, which places the two ketone C=O groups in a 1,5-relationship. This 1,5-diketone pattern is what the Robinson annulation then cyclises.

options: A Michael addition followed by an intramolecular aldol condensation
An aldol condensation followed by a Michael addition
A Knoevenagel condensation followed by decarboxylation
A Claisen condensation followed by a Michael addition
questions.explain: An enolate first adds 1,4 to methyl vinyl ketone to give a 1,5-diketone, and an intramolecular aldol condensation then closes a cyclohexenone ring.
